title: Prefill+Decode cohort fabric and kernel candidate evaluator
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic, cohort-driven harness that evaluates kernel selection heuristics in the context of coordinated prefill+decode scheduling. The harness (cohort fabric) will synthesize traffic mixes across sequence-length cohorts, tokenizer variants, and cache hit/miss states, then run a kernel candidate evaluator to compare latency/cost/accuracy trade-offs across kernel implementations (baseline, quantized, window-optimized). Output artifacts: reproducible golden baselines, per-kernel artifact traces (KV cache profiles, occupancy heatmaps), and CI perf gates with automated regression detection.

Why: Existing microbench and mixbench runs exercise kernels in isolation or via stochastic workload samplers. We need a deterministic, cohort-aware evaluation that surfaces regressions caused by prefills interacting with decoder scheduling and kernel switching at runtime (example: long-prefill then rapid decode bursts). This will reduce late-stage surprises when rolling new kernel routing policies.

Scope:
- Implement cohort fabric that can replay deterministic cohorts (short/medium/long seqs, interactive chat, multi-turn prefill-heavy flows).
- Instrument KV cache state transitions and attach them to trace IDs for correlation.
- Kernel candidate evaluator: run each request through multiple kernel execution variants under identical scheduling/caching conditions and collect side-by-side metrics.
- Golden baseline exporter: pack a lockfile of seeds + pickled cohorts + perf summaries for CI reproducibility.
- CI integration: add perf gate that compares current run against golden baseline with configurable thresholds on p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-token delta.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Cohort fabric can express and replay at least 12 canonical cohorts (config as YAML) with deterministic seed-locking.
2) Kernel candidate evaluator produces a per-request vector of {kernel_id, latency_ms, tokens, kv_cache_reads, cpu_ms, gpu_ms, memory_peak} and stores CSV/NDJSON artifact.
3) Golden baseline exporter generates a lockfile that CI can fetch and use for regression comparisons.
4) One CI perf gate added to runtime-1.19 pipeline validating p99 within 8% and cost-per-token within 10% vs baseline for the 'interactive-long-prefill' cohort.
5) Documentation (Confluence) and a small demo notebook (notebooks/) available for SRE/bench engineers.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Diego Morales: Kickoff - rough design decided in async doc. Chose deterministic seed-locking approach rather than pure replay of prod traces to avoid PII issues and to make CI reproducible. Link to proposal: https://confluence.redwood-inference/pages/COHORT-FABRIC-PROPOSAL

2025-02-21 - Asha Patel: Spike complete. Implemented a minimal cohort YAML and deterministic RNG seeding. Verified identical input streams across runs. PR for seed infra: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1987

2025-02-25 - SRE review (K. Nguyen): Asked for expansion of trace IDs to include region/instance-type to catch HW-specific regressions. Added field to the artifact schema. Updated acceptance criteria to require instance metadata in export.

2025-02-28 - Eng review (R. Singh): Observability checklist reviewed. Agreed that KV cache state snapshots should be limited to meta counters (reads/writes/hits) not raw keys to avoid blowup. Action: implement aggregated counters and heatmap buckets.

2025-03-03 - Asha Patel: Kernel candidate evaluator prototype ran against 3 kernels (baseline, q4-int8, attention-window) across 'interactive-long' cohort. Early findings: q4-int8 shows 12% improvement in p50 but regression in p99 under bursty decode due to suboptimal prefill memory layout. Created issue ENG-427002 to track memory layout mitigation.

2025-03-05 - Diego Morales: CI integration PR opened to runtime pipeline with a draft perf gate. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci/pull/402. Need final thresholds and approval from perf owners before merging.
next_steps: Finish kernel candidate evaluator full-run against expanded cohort set (12 cohorts), finalize artifact schema to include instance metadata, tune CI thresholds with two golden runs, and land CI perf gate after perf-owner signoff.
notes: Trade-offs considered: deterministic cohort playback simplifies CI but may miss rare production noise; decided to add optional stochastic augmentation mode later. We will not capture raw token streams for privacy reasons—only token counts and hashed prefixes. Will coordinate with privacy/compliance if we need deeper traces.
